items.abstract: <jats:p>Forecasting cryptocurrency realized volatility is challenging because market dynamics changeabruptly and predictive signals from prices, transaction networks, and investor sentiment evolve at different rates. We propose R3-MoE (Regime-Routed Residual Mixture of Experts), a multimodal framework for forecasting 24-hour realized volatility. The framework assigns fast technical and on-chain activity signals to a temporal encoder, while slower transaction-graph structure and sentiment provide contextual information. Unlike conventional mixtures of experts that jointly learn a gate and multiple full-output predictors, R3-MoE fits a global predictor to capture structure shared across all observations and trains regime-specific experts only on its residual errors. An external Gaussian mixture model then routes these corrections using lagged log volatility, making the regime signal explicit and available at forecast time. On a chronological Bitcoin test set of 7,096 hourly forecasts, R3-MoE achieved a quasi-likelihood loss of 0.0921, outperforming 12 econometric, machine-learning, and neural baselines and reducing loss by 15.4% relative to the strongest baseline. Across three rolling-origin folds, it ranked first in every fold and reduced mean quasi-likelihood loss by 33.6%. Ablations confirm that the residual decomposition, routing, and role-separated multimodal inputs each contribute to performance. On Ethereum, the framework ranked second among 13 methods while attaining the lowest root mean squared error and highest coefficient of determination. These results indicate that separating shared prediction from regime dependent correction provides an effective and interpretable approach to volatility forecasting under changing market conditions.</jats:p>
title: Regime-Routed Residual Mixture of Experts for Multimodal Bitcoin Realized Volatility Forecasting
